message.reasoning:
We need to parse the logical statement: "Being labeled is required for every sealed parcel." Means: For all x, if x is sealed then x is labeled. Formal: ∀x (Sealed(x) → Labeled(x)). Equivalent: No sealed parcel is unlabeled. So if a particular parcel lacks a label (i.e., ¬Labeled(p)), can we infer ¬Sealed(p)? From contrapositive: ¬Labeled(p) → ¬Sealed(p). The contrapositive of the universal conditional is valid: ∀x (Sealed(x) → Labeled(x)) entails ∀x (¬Labeled(x) → ¬Sealed(x)). So yes, the parcel is not sealed. So answer A.

Thus final line: A.
